approach: Add a pure module `crates/athena-core/src/run/stale_text.rs` that, from a base tree and a new tree, finds text that still says what the change made false, and wire it in at the two places the decision gate already uses. (1) Detection: it takes the lines a change removed and the lines it added, per file (set difference of lines, so a moved line is not a removal). Old values come from a Rust `const`/`static` whose single literal (one number, or one string) changed in the same file. Old claims come from removed comment or prose lines (Rust `//`, `///`, `//!`, `#` in toml, any non-table line of `.md`) of at least 6 words. A value hit is a line in a searched file that holds the old value as a whole token, shares a keyword with the constant's name (generic words like max, min, limit, default dropped), and does not also hold the new value. A claim hit is a run of the same words, ignoring case, punctuation and line wrapping, anywhere in a searched file. Searched files are `.rs .md .toml .yml .yaml .sh` of at most 2 MiB, never CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/`, `.git/`. A hit is dropped when its line is one the diff added, or it sits in a decision entry of docs/decisions.md that says 'amended by'/'superseded by' (any case) or whose id is the `older` of a [[link]] in docs/decision-links.toml (`athena_data::decision_links::link_pairs`), or, outside the log, in a paragraph that says either phrase. A finding is `path:line (D<id> when in the log): still says <old> (<why>): <line text>`. (2) In `producer_loop` (producer.rs:498-556) the check runs next to the decision gate on the work tree; its findings join the all-clear test, the problem list and the send-back brief through a new `append_stale_text` in send_back.rs (modelled on `append_mirror_drift`, send_back.rs:227), and use the one shared send-back (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1, mod.rs:1682). (3) At the candidate (mod.rs, right after the decision gate at mod.rs:2007-2020) the same function runs on base and candidate commits and, if findings remain, closes the job failed before the PR, checks and verifier with reason `stale text left by the change:` plus the list. Both ends call `Athena::stale_text_in_snapshot` / `stale_text_at_candidate` in checks.rs, which read trees with `ls_tree`, `blob_sizes` and chunked `cat_blobs`. (4) Help strings: add `fill_limits` to athena-cli lib.rs and, in `cli_command()` (main.rs:612), fill `{urgent_cap}`, `{high_cap}`, `{repeat_jobs}`, `{improvement_gap}`, `{turn_every}` and `{pending_mins}` placeholders from `DEFAULT_URGENT_CAP`, `DEFAULT_HIGH_CAP` (athena-data config.rs:54-56), `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS`, `IMPROVEMENT_GAP` (plan.rs:466,471) and `athena_gate::attribution::PENDING_WINDOW` (attribution.rs:52), the same way D156 fills `{ceiling}` (main.rs:605-623). (5) Record it as D190 (appended; Amends D156, whose alternative (d) is this follow-up), a `[[link]]` D156 -> D190 amended, one CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Hook the check at the two places the decision gate already uses: `producer_loop` (once, as a send-back) and the candidate step in mod.rs after line 2020 (as a closing failure). One pure function serves both; only the tree reader differs (the snapshot's own git with `work_tree_tree()` and `base()`, or `self.git` with the base and candidate commits).
decisions.reason: This is the existing shape for a finding that must reach the producer in its loop and still stop a job before the verifier: checks.rs:734 `unreconciled_in_snapshot` and checks.rs:697 `unreconciled_decisions`, called at producer.rs:498 and mod.rs:2013. It gives the producer the list inside its loop (criterion 4) and fails the check before the final verdict. It also reuses `Athena::failure`, the `recorded_checks.is_none()` and `nested.is_none()` guards, and the not-an-environment-stop closing (disk.rs:462 `StopCause::of` returns Work for any reason without the environment prefix).

rejected.option: Run it only inside `run_loop_checks` (checks.rs:444) beside the configured checks.
rejected.why: That run is advisory, skipped for low disk, a busy slot or tool config (checks.rs:450-464), and never ends the job, so a skipped run would let stale text reach the verdict.

rejected.option: Run it only at the candidate, as a closing failure.
rejected.why: The producer would see the list only on a retry; the request asks for the list inside the producer's own loop, and D156 (d) names that as the missing step.

rejected.option: Add it to the verifier's gap list (`report_gaps`).
rejected.why: The verifier's judgement is model-based and would make the rule prose, against the mechanism default.

decisions.choice: Detection is textual and conservative: a changed `const`/`static` with one literal (value hits, keyword-gated), and removed comment or prose lines of 6 or more words (claim hits, matched as a word run across wrapped lines). The reading is not parsed.
decisions.reason: The brief puts semantic detection out of scope. Gating a value hit on a shared name keyword stops a changed `8` from flagging every `8` in the repo. A claim must be removed and not re-added anywhere in the diff, which keeps moved comments quiet. The test for the reverse-rule case is a decision that repeats the removed claim; the old claim is what `docs/decisions.md` still says.

rejected.option: Search every number on every removed line.
rejected.why: Most removed numbers are incidental; the search would flood and refuse jobs that changed nothing about a limit.

rejected.option: Read the accepted reading for claims.
rejected.why: The reading is prose from a model with no stable form to match; the diff is the only stable input, and the reading is not available at the candidate step of a resumed job.

decisions.choice: 'Marked' means the decision entry (heading to the next heading) contains 'amended by' or 'superseded by' in any case, or its id is the `older` of a [[link]] in the candidate's docs/decision-links.toml; outside the log it means the blank-line paragraph holds either phrase. CHANGELOG.md is never searched. A line the diff added is never reported.
decisions.reason: That is the brief's exemption rule, and the link list is how this repo records a supersession (decision-links.toml header lines 1-14; the log holds only 4 'superseded by' phrases against many linked pairs). `link_pairs` (decision_links.rs:101) already parses the list; a parse error means no ids are marked, so the check errs towards reporting.

rejected.option: Count only the literal phrase in the entry.
rejected.why: Most older entries are marked only by a link in the toml file, so the check would flag every one of them.

decisions.choice: Exits of the new stage, one line each. Pass (no findings): `stale_text_in_snapshot` returns empty at producer.rs next to line 498; the loop's all-clear test (producer.rs:545) is unchanged in effect; state left: none; read next by the verifier path. Fail with a send-back left: `send_backs += 1` at producer.rs:676, the problem line joins `problems`, `append_stale_text` adds the section to `attempt_brief` (producer.rs:701), state is the brief; read next by the next producer pass, which runs the check again. Fail at the limit: the `send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` branch (producer.rs:635) prints `producer   stale text still left after the send-back; the job ends before the verifier` and breaks with the report; the stale list is not added to `report_problems` (the job ends at the candidate); state: work tree with the text; read next by `stale_text_at_candidate`. Fail at the candidate: new block in mod.rs after line 2020 does `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &reason)` keeping `changed_paths` and `verification_passed = None` like mod.rs:2014-2018; state: Failed outcome with reason prefix `stale text left by the change:`; read next by close/records, `athena retry` (which starts a fresh producer whose loop reruns the check; `retry_findings` at retry.rs:489-493 does not carry this reason, so the retry brief omits it, and the loop supplies the list). Error (tree unreadable, git failure): both entry points return empty and print `producer   stale text not checked: <why>` (the policy of `settle_loop_checks`, checks.rs:432-441: an advisory step never discards finished work); state: none. Hold: cannot happen, the check takes no slot and reads no disk gate. Interrupt: cannot happen inside the check (a bounded read of git objects, no agent or process wait); the kill switch is read by the producer invocation before it and by `refuse_if_stopped` at the next stage. Skipped without a line: `self.nested.is_some()`, an empty change list, and a resume at the verifier stage (`recorded_checks.is_some()`), the same guards as the decision gate.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for every exit of a new stage; each row names the file:line that handles it, the state it leaves and the code that reads it next.

rejected.option: Treat a read error as a finding.
rejected.why: A git read failure says nothing about the work; it would fail jobs for the environment.

risks.risk: False positives: an unrelated line holding the old number, or a removed comment whose words survive in a document, fail a job that changed nothing false.
risks.mitigation: Value hits need a shared keyword from the constant's name plus the old value as a whole token, and skip lines that also hold the new value. Claims need 6 or more words, must be comment or prose lines, and must not be re-added anywhere in the diff. Output is capped at 30 findings with a count of the rest. Tests cover a non-matching 8 and a moved comment. The refusal rate is an estimate (brief: 10%), not measured.

risks.risk: Reading every text file of the tree at each producer pass costs time and memory on a large repository.
risks.mitigation: Search only text extensions, skip files over 2 MiB and CHANGELOG.md, read blobs in chunks of 200 with one `cat-file --batch` (as planning.rs does), and read base text only for changed paths. A failed read is a skip line, not a failure.

risks.risk: A decision that restates the old rule in other words, or a heading that moves, is missed or mis-marked.
risks.mitigation: The wrap-tolerant word-run match and the entry/paragraph rule are covered by tests with a wrapped sentence and with the three marking forms; the brief puts semantic matching out of scope, so a reworded reversal is not caught and the D190 Tradeoff says so.

risks.risk: The new decision entry or the CHANGELOG entry trips the ontology rule, the append-only rule or the banned-word scan.
risks.mitigation: The producer must run `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` after writing D190; the plan keeps D190's prose free of ontology term definitions and adds the entry only at the end of the file.

risks.risk: A clap doc comment's text is stored as `about` or `long_about` depending on its paragraphs, so a fill that reads the wrong getter leaves a placeholder in the help.
risks.mitigation: Keep `fill_limits` generic and test each filled string against its constant; if clap derive gives a one-paragraph doc comment only an `about` and no `long_about`, the helper fills whichever of about, long about and after_help exists. Check `jiff::SignedDuration::as_mins` for `PENDING_WINDOW` when building; if absent use `as_secs() / 60`.

risks.risk: A retry brief omits the stale-text finding because `retry_findings` (retry.rs:489-493) is not extended.
risks.mitigation: The retry's own producer loop reruns the check and supplies the list in its first send-back (shown by the loop test); recorded in the D190 Tradeoff.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `stale_text::tests::a_constant_raised_from_8_to_16_names_the_help_line_still_saying_8` builds an in-memory `Input`: a changed file `crates/core/src/limits.rs` whose old text has `pub const MAX_WIDGETS: u32 = 8;` and new text `= 16;`, and a searched file `crates/cli/src/main.rs` with the line `/// Runs at most 8 widgets per job.` on a known line. It calls `find` and asserts one `Stale` with that path, that line number, old value `8`, and a Display text that contains `crates/cli/src/main.rs:<line>`. A second case in the same test: a line `/// Takes 8 seconds.` with no shared keyword is not reported.
demonstrations.observes: The finding names the file and line of the help string; unrelated 8s are not reported.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `find` returning an empty list (the check not implemented or not run), the test's assert that the finding list is exactly one entry at `crates/cli/src/main.rs:<line>` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `stale_text::find(&Input)`, a pure function over plain data (`files: BTreeMap<path, text>`, `changed: [Changed{path, old, new}]`, `links: &str`). No fake or double: the fixture is the data. The seam is added by plan step 1.

demonstrations.method: Test `stale_text::tests::a_decision_that_says_the_removed_rule_and_is_not_marked_is_named_with_its_id_and_line` uses a changed doc comment that goes from `/// A retry keeps the work of the failed attempt for the next producer.` to `/// A retry discards the work of the failed attempt and starts from the base.`, and a `docs/decisions.md` text with `## D45 · Retries` and, wrapped over two lines, the sentence `a retry keeps the work of the failed` / `attempt for the next producer`. `find` must return a finding whose path is docs/decisions.md, with decision id `D45` and the line of the first wrapped line. A variant with `(superseded by D99)` in the entry, and a variant with a toml link older = D45, return none.
demonstrations.observes: The unmarked decision is named by id and line; marked entries are not.
demonstrations.fails_without: If decision-log matching or claim extraction were missing, `find` returns nothing for the log and the assert on the D-id and line fails. A second case shows the entry becomes quiet only when marked, so the test fails if the marked-entry rule is ignored in the other direction.
demonstrations.seam: `stale_text::find(&Input)`, same seam as criterion 1, with the log text as one entry of `files` and the toml text in `links`. Added by plan step 1.

demonstrations.method: Test `stale_text::tests::both_fixtures_pass_once_the_text_is_updated_and_exempt_places_are_not_reported` re-runs the two fixtures with the help line changed to 16 and the decision entry changed to the new rule (so the added lines are in the diff), and asserts `find` is empty. It then adds, to one fixture, an old-value line in CHANGELOG.md (never in `files`, as `read_tree` leaves it out; asserted separately by a `read_tree` test over a temporary git repository holding CHANGELOG.md with the old value), a marked entry, and a line the diff added that holds the old value, and asserts none is reported. An end-to-end test in run/tests.rs, `stale_text_send_back_fix_lets_the_job_reach_the_verifier`, uses `governed_job_with(&repo, script)` where the repo has `src/limits.rs` (`MAX_WIDGETS: u32 = 8`) and `HELP.md` (`at most 8 widgets`), the script (built from `editing`, tests.rs:3567) sets the constant to 16 on the first pass and, when `spec.user_prompt` contains `## Sent back`, also fixes HELP.md; the job reaches the verifier and lands.
demonstrations.observes: Updated text passes; exempt places stay quiet; a producer that fixes the text after the send-back lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the exemptions the 'passes once updated' assertions fail (the diff-added line, the marked entry and the CHANGELOG line would be reported); without the update path the fixtures would still fail, so the same tests show both directions.
demonstrations.seam: `stale_text::find` and `stale_text::read_tree` (added in plan step 1); the end-to-end test drives `Athena::go` through `FakeAgentDriver` with the `athena_agent::fake::Script` that exists (tests.rs:192-225, 3596) and `commit_file` (tests.rs:359) to seed the repository; no new double.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs: `stale_text_is_sent_back_to_the_producer_before_verification` runs the job above with an `editing`-style script that records prompts; asserts prompts[1] contains `## Sent back`, the section heading `Stale text`, `HELP.md:1`, and the old value; counts (producer, verifier) are (2, 1) and the UI shows `producer   sent back: stale text`. `stale_text_left_after_the_send_back_ends_the_job_before_the_verifier` uses a script that never fixes HELP.md and asserts state Failed, reason starting `stale text left by the change:` and naming `HELP.md:1`, counts (2, 0), no `checks     ` or `verifier   ` line, and `!crate::disk::is_environment_reason(&done.reason)`. Reviewers also read `git diff -- crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/send_back.rs` for the call sites.
demonstrations.observes: The list is in the producer's second brief; an unfixed change ends before the verifier.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `producer_loop` did not call the check or did not append its list, the second prompt would not contain the finding and the producer count would be 1 (job accepted with stale text); if the candidate gate were missing, the job with an unfixed producer would reach the verifier (verifier count 1).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` (via `governed_job_with`, tests.rs:3596) over `producer_loop` (producer.rs:298) and the candidate step (mod.rs:1964); fixture is the existing `FakeAgentDriver` script; guards: `nested.is_none()`, a non-empty change list, `recorded_checks.is_none()`. Exists today; only the two scripts are new.

demonstrations.method: New tests in main.rs beside `drain_help_follows_the_ceiling_it_is_built_from` (main.rs:1511): `plan_help_states_the_caps_the_config_enforces` renders `cli_command()`'s `plan` long help (whitespace joined) and asserts it contains `format!("default {DEFAULT_URGENT_CAP} urgent, {DEFAULT_HIGH_CAP} high")`, `format!("{REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS} or more distinct jobs")` and no `{`; `limit_templates_carry_placeholders_not_numbers` reads the derived (unfilled) text of `plan`, `drain` and `check` and asserts the placeholders are present and the old literals are absent; `fill_limits` in lib.rs has a unit test over several values (as the ceiling test does) and asserts only the number changes. The diff of crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs shows each string and constant.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --bin athena help && cargo test -p athena-cli --lib fill_limits
demonstrations.observes: Each help string that restates a limit shows the constant's value and follows it.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old literal text in the doc comments, the template tests (`template.contains("{urgent_cap}")`, `!template.contains("default 3 urgent")`) fail; with a template that is not filled, the filled-help test fails on the surviving placeholder; and a filled help that did not follow its constant would fail the loop over test values.
demonstrations.seam: `cli_command()` (main.rs:612, the function `main` runs at main.rs:640) and `athena_cli::fill_limits` (added in plan step 5); the constants are the real ones; no double.

demonstrations.method: `git diff -- docs/decisions.md docs/decision-links.toml` shows only appended lines in the log (new `## D190 · ` entry with Provenance) and one `[[link]]` D156 -> D190 amended in the toml; the four test commands read the real files.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core mirrors && cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors && cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest && cargo test -p athena-data decision_links
demonstrations.observes: The log stays append-only and well formed, and the link resolves.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the entry were edited into an old one the `AppendOnly` rule (mirrors.rs:121) fails; a missing Provenance bullet fails `DecisionEntries`; an 'Amends D156' phrase with no link, or an unneeded link, fails `link_problems` and the backtest.
demonstrations.seam: Real files read by the existing mirror, backtest and decision-link checks (`mirrors::check_all`, `athena_data::decision_links`); nothing new.

demonstrations.method: Read the added `### Added` bullet under `## [Unreleased]`: it names the check (`crates/athena-core/src/run/stale_text.rs`), the in-loop send-back and the candidate close, the help strings built from constants, D190, the limits (textual match only, 6-word claims, keyword-gated values) and the tests, and nothing else.
demonstrations.observes: One entry, and each claim in it matches a part of the diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: An entry that claims more than the diff does (for example a refusal rate or a measure not made) would contradict the diff the verifier reads; `changelog_required` (admission.rs, used at producer.rs:474) would also refuse a missing entry.
demonstrations.seam: None; a content criterion read from the diff. `cargo test -p athena-core changelog` is also run for the admission rule.

demonstrations.method: Run the three recorded checks on the final tree, and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-core run::`, `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test -p xtask`. I did not run them and cite no result.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All pass; the corpus is unchanged because the new rule reads diffs, not readings.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any existing test that the new check or the help change breaks (the run tests that drive `producer_loop`, `settle_loop_checks` at tests.rs:6252, the pin tests in run_pin_tests.rs, the main.rs help tests) fails the run; `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` shows no reading refusal changed, because this plan touches no reading code.
demonstrations.seam: The real test suite; the existing fake-agent harness (tests.rs:180-225).

demonstrations.method: The stat lists only: stale_text.rs, run/mod.rs, producer.rs, checks.rs, send_back.rs, run/tests.rs, athena-cli lib.rs and main.rs, docs/decisions.md, docs/decision-links.toml, CHANGELOG.md. No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, Cargo file or crates/athena-data file changes, since every constant used already exists and is `pub`. Existing behavior: with no changed constant or removed claim the check returns nothing, shown by the unchanged existing run tests.
demonstrations.observes: Scope is the deliverables plus main.rs (see open question).
demonstrations.fails_without: A change to any file outside the list would show in the stat.

open_questions: User: Criterion 5 and criterion 9 pull in different directions: the help strings live in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, which is not in the brief's deliverable list, and criterion 9 says no other file changes. This plan edits main.rs (and only that file beyond the list), because criterion 5 asks for the diff of the file where each string lives. Say if you want main.rs left alone; then criterion 5 would hold only for the `fill_limits` helper in lib.rs and the help strings would stay literal.
